ov: The western jackdaw, a small, gregarious member of the crow family, black with a grey nape and striking pale eyes. Jackdaws are intelligent, have been seen using tools, and are monogamous, nesting in holes in trees, cliffs and buildings.
rg: Europe, western Asia and western North Africa.
df: Almost anything: plants, invertebrates and food waste from towns.
fx: Linnaeus named it monedula, from the Latin for money, because of its supposed fondness for picking up coins.
A flock of jackdaws was once called a "clattering".
